text: DISCHARGE SUMMARY CHIEF COMPLAINT: Dysuria, flank pain, and low-grade fever. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 64-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease presents with acute urinary tract infection symptoms. LABS: Urinalysis shows 50-100 WBCs/hpf, moderate bacteria. Urine culture grew E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin. Serum creatinine stable at 1.4 mg/dL. COURSE: Completed 3-day course of intravenous ceftriaxone, transitioned to oral cefdinir with complete resolution of dysuria and fever. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: 1. Urinary tract infection, site not specified. 2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications. 3. Chronic kidney disease, unspecified.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY CHIEF COMPLAINT: Progressive breathlessness and leg swelling. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: An 80-year-old male with chronic kidney disease, stage 3 and hypertension presents with congestive heart failure exacerbation. EXAM & LABS: Elevated JVP, bibasilar rales, BNP 1,890 pg/mL. Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL. COURSE: Intravenous loop diuretics administered with 4 kg negative fluid balance over 4 days. Orthopnea resolved. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: 1. Heart failure, unspecified. 2. Chronic kidney disease, stage 3 (moderate). 3. Essential (primary) hypertension.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY CHIEF COMPLAINT: Severe shortness of breath and blue lips. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 70-year-old female with severe COPD admitted with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure following a viral respiratory illness. VITAL SIGNS: SpO2 84% on room air, RR 32 bpm. Arterial blood gas confirmed severe hypoxia with PaO2 52 mmHg. COURSE: Required non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (BiPAP), systemic corticosteroids, and nebulized ipratropium/albuterol. Weaned to 2L cannula prior to discharge. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: 1. Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia. 2. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation.
